weather_line: Southeast fog lifting slowly · ducks watching

stories.headline: The Orange Duck Bears a Number: '7' Stamped Beneath Its Left Wing; No Registry Exists; the Bandit Knows Something
body: A development of material significance was reported this morning when Steve, conducting his routine pre-ignition inspection, turned the orange duck over in his hand for the first time and found, stamped in faint black ink beneath its left wing, the numeral 7. The mark is precise, not accidental — the stamp's edges are clean, the ink aged by perhaps a week, consistent with preparation before placement.

Cross-referencing with the expedition chart has produced one unsettling alignment: the unnamed tributary that feeds Harlan's Creek crosses the survey grid at marker seven, approximately forty yards below the point where Christine held her line during the crossing on the first of August. Whether the Bandit was present that morning, whether they have access to the survey, or whether the numeral arrived at its meaning independently — these questions are, as yet, unanswered.

The original duck continues to face north-northeast. The orange duck faces southeast. The forty-seven degrees between them has not changed. Lucy, according to Steve's margin note filed with the subcommittee at half nine, 'circled the Jeep twice and then sat facing the road for eleven minutes.' She has not explained herself.

stories.headline: Three Disputed Accounts Resolved Before the Lunch Bell; a Fourth Attempts Dispute; Is Advised to Reconsider
body: Wednesday's morning session at Gringotts concluded with the resolution of three accounts flagged as 'historically intractable' — a designation the bank's senior clerks regard as permanent and Christine regards as a scheduling matter. All three were closed, annotated, and filed before the third-floor lunch cart made its first pass.

A fourth account presented itself at eleven forty-seven, its holder arriving with documentation and what witnesses described as 'considerable confidence.' Christine reviewed the documents for ninety seconds, asked one clarifying question, and suggested the account-holder might wish to review clause fourteen before proceeding. The account-holder reviewed clause fourteen. The account-holder thanked her. The account was, upon reflection, fine.

stories.headline: Subcommittee Requests That the Numeral 7 Be Added to Its Jurisdiction; Learns Jurisdiction Does Not Work That Way; Adjourns to Draft a Proposal Explaining Why It Should
body: The Ministry's Duck Subcommittee met for forty minutes this morning following receipt of Steve's margin note and convened in what its chair described as 'a state of focused agitation.' The discovery of the stamped numeral was entered into evidence as Exhibit D, the preceding three exhibits being the duck itself (A), its southeast orientation (B), and the forty-seven-degree angle (C, filed Tuesday, cross-referenced to the survey grid this morning for the first time with results the subcommittee described as 'concerning in the best possible way').

A motion was raised to extend the subcommittee's jurisdiction to include all stamped numerals found on enchanted waterfowl within a half-mile radius of the Jeep. The motion passed unanimously. The Ministry's Office of Magical Boundaries subsequently informed the subcommittee that jurisdiction does not function via internal motion. The subcommittee has requested two weeks to draft a counter-proposal and has in the meantime simply begun treating the numeral as within its remit regardless.

stories.headline: Steve Files Winch Maintenance Log; Jeep Deemed Trail-Ready; the Jeep Accepts This Assessment With Quiet Dignity
body: Steve completed the winch maintenance log Wednesday morning, the final item outstanding from the Harlan's Hollow expedition. All components are serviced, the recovery line re-spooled to specification, and the Jeep — which has been facing the road since its return on the first — has been described in Steve's log as 'ready when she is.' Observers note the Jeep's expression has not changed, as it is a Jeep, but that it nevertheless conveys quiet satisfaction.

The flint stone from Keeps Ridge remains at the head of the kitchen table. The chart is still folded on its new mark. No further margin words have been added, though Steve was seen standing in the kitchen for several minutes this evening holding a pencil and looking at the fold.

familiars_corner: Lucy: filed no formal report this morning, which the subcommittee has logged as more alarming than if she had; her eleven minutes facing the road remain uncharacterised and she has declined all comment.

Ellie: discovered the orange duck's reflection in the Jeep's door panel and introduced herself to it at length; the introduction went well; she has plans to introduce the reflection to the original duck tomorrow and sees no complications.

Jersey: completed an extended assessment of Steve's lap during the winch-log review, found it fully satisfactory, and has submitted his findings as an endorsement of all future maintenance sessions conducted in the same position.
founding_editor_note: The number seven is on the underside because that's where you put the mark that matters — I did the same thing with every third-floor joist, and I was always right. — D.

in_brief.sport: Wednesday training logged; the weights, as always, did their best and came off second.
in_brief.forecast: Southeast fog holding through evening; the forty-seven-degree corridor between ducks remains open; something is coming from that direction, though it has not yet said when.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Waits
storyline_updates.summary: Day 2: The orange duck has been found to bear the numeral 7 stamped beneath its left wing — clean, precise, aged about a week. Survey marker 7 sits on the Harlan's Creek tributary grid, forty yards below Christine's crossing line. The alignment may be coincidental; no one believes it is. Lucy circled the Jeep twice and sat facing the road for eleven minutes. The Ministry subcommittee has claimed jurisdiction over the numeral by internal motion, which is not how jurisdiction works. The forty-seven-degree angle between ducks is unchanged. Day 3 should produce either a glimpse of the Bandit — a figure seen at the edge of the drive, a second token left near the Jeep, or a connection established between the numeral 7 and someone who was known to be near the creek on the morning of the first — or a second stamped numeral, somewhere unexpected, deepening the trail.
